body.x: BarunBio, a corporation headed by CEO Hong Jin-ki, participated in CES 2024, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics expo, held in Las Vegas from January 9 to 12.

Specializing in anti-aging life care, BarunBio has introduced advanced athleisure clothing to the market. Leveraging over a decade of research and development, the company has successfully developed functional clothing that maximizes user performance using micro-electric energy technology.

The ‘WE-STIM’ leggings by BarunBio, unveiled at CES 2024, are characterized by the use of micro-electricity generated from everyday movements, eliminating the need for separate batteries or electronic components. The company explains that this harvested energy is delivered to the user’s muscles, promoting continuous functional activation.

During CES 2024, BarunBio showcased its WE-STIM leggings as the flagship product. The leggings deliver electrical stimulation to the muscles, enhancing performance by up to 30% and reducing muscle fatigue by 6%, according to experiments conducted by the company. Additionally, based on the tangible effects of WE-STIM leggings, BarunBio received an innovation award in the wearable technology category at CES.

body.cap: BarunBio representatives presented their WE-STIM athleisure clothing product line to global attendees at CES 2024, held in Las Vegas on January 9 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Hong Jin-ki, CEO of BarunBio, stated, “Participating in the international stage of CES allowed us to collect feedback from diverse groups, ranging from multinational healthcare industry professionals to general attendees.” He added, “The experience helped us gain new insights that can be applied to developing next-generation solutions, including improvement areas not previously considered internally.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
